title: One-page pitch: why a community makerspace needs a CNC router
summary: A makerspace pitch built around access, supervised use and an explicit operating budget.

blocks.heading: Fund access to making larger, repeatable parts
blocks.body: Approve a six-month CNC router pilot if the makerspace can confirm a suitable room, dust collection, trained supervision and an operating budget. Members could make fixtures, signs and flat-pack furniture while learning the path from drawing to finished part.

blocks.heading: Illustrative first-year envelope
blocks.caption: Fictional planning allowances, not vendor quotes. Confirm electrical, ventilation, noise, insurance and access requirements before purchase.

blocks.heading: What shared ownership buys
blocks.body: A member with a one-off project does not need a machine in their garage. The space provides a supervised route through file review, toolpath preparation, workholding and inspection. A completed cut is only one part of the service; instruction and safe setup are the value.

blocks.heading: Make the pilot earn expansion
rows: Project records with material, time and outcome
The hourly charge covers measured running costs
Consumables, supervision and maintenance tracked separately
Booking wait time and scholarship use reviewed
blocks.caption: These are proposed targets, not reported results.

blocks.heading: The machine cannot be its own operator
blocks.body: Name a program owner and trained supervisors before ordering. If staffing or extraction cannot be sustained, use a partner shop for the pilot and revisit ownership after demand is demonstrated.
